trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha gave back a little more ground over the past week, with the USD/ZMW market mid at ~K19.6263/USD (open.er-api.com, 1 Oct) versus ~K19.49 a week earlier — a modest ~0.7% softening driven by end-of-quarter import demand and the 10% copper-concentrate export duty taking effect on 30 September. The move was basket-wide but shallow: GBP (26.0743, +0.72%), CNY (2.9386, +0.85%) and ZAR (1.2001, +0.5%) all cost marginally more ZMW, while EUR (22.306, +0.27%) and BWP (1.3914, +0.05%) were effectively unchanged — a mild, basket-wide softening rather than a sharp single-pair move. The pair still sits inside its broad 18.40–19.80 consolidation band. The headline policy event was the BoZ's 250bps MPR cut to 10.75% on 30 September as inflation returned inside target; a lower policy rate trims the carry attractiveness that supported the kwacha earlier in 2026, even as the IMF successor-programme talks and the 2027 budget process shape the medium-term outlook.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 18.50–19.80 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.00–20.00 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
